review_style.value: LLM review before any human review
review_style.quote: Nuclear opinion: I don’t care if you use AI to write code,¹ but making a human review a change before an LLM is disrespectful.

also.quote: I’m saying if you ask human attention, do an LLM review first.
Importantly, there is no need to trust the LLM or review its output when its job is just saving me an hour or two by telling me where the bug is, for me to reason about it and fix it.
The level of testing and review they are enabling in the Go cryptography standard library is amazing.

rules_files.value: AGENTS.md with Go CLI tips (personal, shown as an image)
rules_files.quote: Here are three lines from my AGENTS.md that make agents a lot better with Go.

signature.caption: agent's own GitHub account
signature.why: Our pick: his agent commits from a separate, low-privilege GitHub account so it never holds his maintainer keys.
signature.quote: I don’t want to “install Claude” with all the privileges of my account, I want Claude to have its own account to which I will grant some permissions, or none at all because again issues and PRs are public!

archetype.why: Fences his agent into its own account and VMs, then has it build tools like muzoo, goapi and gh-pr-rebase.

signature_quote.value: Why am I catching your bugs if a computer could have done it?
signature_quote.more: It’s like asking to review code that doesn’t compile or pass CI.
